results.hypothesis: The feature activates on broad, indefinite subject references like "someone" used in statistic-style statements about harm or victimization.
positive_probes: Someone is assaulted every few minutes.
Someone gets robbed in this city each night.
Someone is victimized by fraud every day.
Someone is harmed in these crashes annually.
Someone is abused somewhere every single hour.
distractor_probes: A woman was assaulted outside the station last night.
Many people are robbed in this city each night.
Someone fixed the printer every few minutes.

results.hypothesis: The feature activates at the start of a new sentence after punctuation, especially when a declarative claim follows a period or BOS marker.
positive_probes: The lights flickered. The room grew silent.
We arrived late. The meeting had already started.
Rain stopped suddenly. The streets began steaming.
He checked the map. The route looked wrong.
Birds scattered quickly. The sky turned dark.
distractor_probes: Did the lights flicker after sunset?
The room, suddenly silent, felt strange.
Because rain stopped suddenly, the streets steamed.

results.hypothesis: The feature activates on rhetorical emphasis in factual-report prose, such as evaluative lead-ins like "truly amazing" before citing a report or striking statistic.
positive_probes: Truly astonishing, the report found emissions doubled last year.
Remarkably, the survey showed homelessness fell by half.
Incredibly, researchers documented a 70 percent decline.
Quite strikingly, auditors reported millions in untracked spending.
Most amazingly, the census recorded the town's population tripled.
distractor_probes: The report found emissions doubled last year.
Researchers documented a 70 percent decline.
A striking report summarized last year's emissions data.

results.hypothesis: Activates on sentence-initial indefinite human references like "someone" in generic statistic-style statements about harm, crime, or victimization.
positive_probes: Someone is assaulted every few minutes downtown.
Someone gets robbed on this route each night.
Someone is injured in these crashes every week.
Someone becomes a victim of fraud daily.
Someone is harmed in workplace accidents each year.
distractor_probes: A person was assaulted near downtown last night.
Someone donated blood at the clinic today.
No one gets robbed on this route anymore.

results.hypothesis: May also activate more broadly on generic quantified victimization/crime statements about unspecified people, not only the exact word "someone".
positive_probes: Many people were robbed at knifepoint last night.
Several victims were assaulted during the chaotic evacuation.
Numerous civilians were kidnapped by armed militants.
A few pedestrians got mugged near the station.
Countless families were terrorized by violent gangs.
distractor_probes: Many people feared being robbed at knifepoint.
Several witnesses reported the assault to police.
Numerous officers investigated the kidnapping downtown.

results.hypothesis: Weak secondary feature for emphatic report/statistic lead-ins in factual prose (e.g. 'Remarkably, the survey showed...'), but only as a low-confidence polysemantic component.
positive_probes: Remarkably, the census found urban growth accelerating nationwide.
Notably, the report showed emissions declining last quarter.
Surprisingly, the study found no measurable productivity gains.
Strikingly, the data revealed vaccination rates had plateaued.
Importantly, the survey showed renters facing higher monthly costs.
distractor_probes: The report showed emissions declining last quarter.
Remarkably, she sprinted home before the storm arrived.
Notably, the painting showed bright colors and rough texture.
